units.title: Unity in Diversity
units.intro: Grammar: active and passive (2): the present and past continuous and the present and past perfect passive.

lessons.title: Passive in continuous and perfect tenses

cards.title: Passive in continuous and perfect tenses
rule: **Present continuous passive:** am/is/are + **being** + past participle: *The road **is being repaired**.*
**Past continuous passive:** was/were + **being** + pp: *The hall **was being cleaned** when we arrived.*
**Present perfect passive:** has/have + **been** + pp: *The results **have been published**.* **Past perfect passive:** had + **been** + pp: *The tickets **had been sold** before we came.*

examples.text: A new school is being built in our village.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **BeING for continuING; BeEN for perfect (havE BEEN).**

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Continuous passives add being (is/was being + pp); perfect passives add been (has/have/had been + pp). The tense of the active sentence stays the same in the passive.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: I failed the national biology matriculation exam; I ________ harder instead of wasting my time on social media.

steps.text: The context 'I failed...; I [blank] harder' indicates a past regret or criticism of an action that was advisable but did not happen.
This requires the past regret modal structure ($$\text{should have} + \text{V}_3$$).
Students often confuse 'must have studied' (logical deduction of fact) with 'should have studied' (regret).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: According to the laboratory safety rules, you ________ enter the chemistry room without wearing safety goggles.

steps.text: The context describes a strict laboratory safety rule.
This requires a modal of prohibition to show the action is forbidden ($$\text{must not} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).
Students often confuse 'don't have to' (lack of obligation/optional) with 'must not' (prohibition/forbidden).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Aster has been studying and living in London for ten years, so she ________ speak English very fluently.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context presents strong present evidence ('living in London for ten years'). This requires a modal of present logical deduction to show high certainty ($$\text{must} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students sometimes choose 'must have' (Option D), but 'must have' is for past deduction ($$\text{must have} + \text{V}_3$$) and cannot be followed by the base verb 'speak'. Option A is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ኣብ ህልው እዋን ዘሎ ናይ ምርግጋጽ ስነ-ሞጎት (present logical deduction) የርእየና። 'ዓሰርተ ዓመት ኣብ ሎንዶን ስለ ዝነበረት' ዝብል መርትዖ ስለ ዘሎ፡ 'ብርግጽ ብጽቡቕ ትዛረብ እያ' ንምባል 'must' (Option A) ክንጥቀም ኣለና። 'must have' ግን ንሕሉፍ እዋን ጥራይ እዩ ዘገልግል።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The soccer field is completely covered in puddles; it ________ heavily during the night.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The present evidence 'The soccer field is completely covered in puddles' leads to a strong positive deduction about a past event. This requires 'must have' ($$\text{must have} + \text{V}_3$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse 'should have rained' (past regret/unrealized advice) with 'must have rained' (past deduction of fact). Option A is incorrect because we are deducing a fact based on physical evidence, making Option B correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'እቲ ናይ ኲዕሶ እግሪ ሜዳ ብማይ ተሸፊኑ ኣሎ' ዝብል ናይ ዓይኒ መርትዖ ስለ ዘለና፡ 'ትማሊ ምሸት ብርግጽ ዓቢ ዝናብ ዘኒቡ ክኸውን ኣለዎ' (past logical deduction) ንምባል 'must have rained' (Option B) ክንመርጽ ኣለና። 'should have' ግን ጣዕሳ ጥራይ እዩ ዝገልጽ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Haile should have sold the car after possessing it for ten years. (Choose the appropriate passive voice)

options.A: The car should have been sold after been possessed by Haile for ten years.
options.B: After being possessed for ten years, the car should be sold by Haile.
options.C: The car should have been sold after being possessed by Haile for ten years.
options.D: The car should have been sold after being possessed for Haile for ten years.
options.E: The car shall be sold after being possessed by Haile for ten years.

cards.why: The active structure 'should have sold' (modal + have + V3) becomes 'should have been sold' in passive. 'Possessing it' (gerund) becomes 'being possessed' (passive gerund).

tips.text: **BeING for continuING; BeEN for perfect (havE BEEN).**
